title: Function Definition and Notation
notes: **Definition.** A function f: A → B assigns to every x ∈ A exactly one value f(x) ∈ B; A is the domain and the set of attained values is the range, a subset of B.
**Notation.** f(x) is the output at input x, not a product; f(a) means substitute a for x wherever the rule is valid at a.
**Domain restrictions.** Exclude zero denominators, negative even roots and non-positive logarithm arguments; the domain fixes which limits and one-sided approaches are meaningful.
**Piecewise rules.** When different formulas apply on different intervals, evaluate each branch separately and pay special attention to the boundary point where the rule changes.
**Worked example.** For f(x) = (x² − 1)/(x − 1), f(1) is undefined but the rule simplifies to x + 1 for x ≠ 1, so the graph is a line with a single hole at (1, 2).
**Exam caution.** A function is not fully specified until its domain is stated; f(x) = x² on ℝ and on [0, ∞) are different functions with different inverses.
summary: A function assigns exactly one output to each input in its domain; f(x) notation, domain, range and piecewise rules fix what a limit question is asking.
